lead:
Keerthi K P (born April 22, 2006) is an Indian software developer, cybersecurity researcher, and Capture The Flag (CTF) competitor. She is currently pursuing a Bachelor of Engineering in Computer Science and Engineering with a specialization in Cybersecurity and Honors in Artificial Intelligence at R.M.D. Engineering College.

Keerthi has interned with the Tamil Nadu Police Cyber Crime Wing, where she helped streamline complex malware analysis tools for non-technical users. As a hackathon and CTF competitor, she was the runner-up in the TCS CodeVita Season 13 Best Women Coder category{{ref:toi}} and has actively organized and placed in various cybersecurity competitions.

sections.title: Terminology
sections.content:
Some of the technical terms on this page may be unfamiliar, so here is a short guide.

  • Capture The Flag (CTF): a cybersecurity competition built around simulated attacks and challenges. Participants solve them to earn points and climb the leaderboard.
  • Hackathon: a technical competition, typically lasting around 24 hours, in which teams build something to solve a problem.
  • Open-source intelligence (OSINT): a cybersecurity term for finding out a name, place, animal, thing or other detail using only publicly available information. It is considered beginner friendly, and many people do it without even realising.

sections.title: Early life and education
sections.content:
Keerthi was introduced to computer science early in her schooling, developing an interest in technology by exploring basic system configurations and educational software. She completed her secondary school certificate (SSC) examinations with 92% and subsequently pursued the Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics (PCM) track combined with Computer Science in higher secondary school (HSC) at Velammal Vidyalaya, completing it in May 2023 with 87%. For her HSC practicals, she built a MySQL-backed command-line password manager, which marked the beginning of her interest in cybersecurity.

She later enrolled at R.M.D. Engineering College in August 2023 to pursue a Bachelor of Engineering in Computer Science and Engineering. Her specialization is Cybersecurity, and she is also pursuing Honors in Artificial Intelligence. She is expected to graduate in 2027, with a current CGPA of 8.62.

subsections.title: Tamil Nadu Police Cyber Crime Wing
subsections.content:
{{image:images/ccw.jpg|Tamil Nadu Police Cyber Crime Wing internship certificate|right|300}}

From June to July 2026, Keerthi interned at the Tamil Nadu Police Cyber Crime Wing in Ashok Nagar, Chennai, focusing on a malware analysis tool for Android APK files. Commuting daily to Ashok Nagar between 11 AM and 5 PM using MTC buses and the Chennai Metro, she noted that navigating the city provided her with as much real-world learning as the internship itself. During her tenure, she redesigned the tool's frontend to improve usability for non-technical police personnel, simplifying complex malware analysis results into an intuitive interface to reduce information overload.

The tool is published in the repository as AndroidSentinel{{ref:androidsentinel}}, a full-stack platform for static and dynamic analysis of Android APK files, modeled on industry tools such as MobSF and Any.Run. Its frontend is a Next.js 14 application written in TypeScript with Tailwind CSS, with an upload page, a live analysis dashboard and a full report viewer, and it talks to a FastAPI backend over REST and WebSocket.

  • Static analysis: APK and DEX parsing with Androguard, YARA rule scanning, permission auditing, embedded URL extraction and optional MobSF integration
  • Dynamic analysis: Frida instrumentation, ADB-based runtime monitoring on an Android emulator, filesystem snapshot comparison and network packet capture (PCAP)
  • Reporting: threat scoring, verdict generation and downloadable PDF and JSON reports
  • Technologies: Python, FastAPI, Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Frida, YARA, SQLite/PostgreSQL

subsections.title: Infosys Springboard
subsections.content:
{{image:images/infy.jpg|Infosys Springboard certificate of completion|right|300}}

From December 2024 to February 2025, Keerthi interned at Infosys Springboard as a Python Developer, where she contributed to an expense management and tracking module for the Unified Family Finance Tracker. The platform supported 5 user profiles and more than 10 expense categories, and was built with Python, Flask and MySQL. In this role, she acted as a Project Manager for a 5-member team and a Scrum Master for a 25-member team to lead the agile delivery of the platform.

{{video:https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/059bb3ae-5fbe-45ca-9285-b32162fb9bce|Demonstration of the Unified Family Finance Tracker from Infosys Springboard.|left}}
  • Project: Unified Family Finance Tracker, an expense management and tracking platform for families
  • Scope: 5 user profiles and more than 10 expense categories
  • Technologies: Python, Flask, MySQL
  • Roles: Project Manager (5-member team) and Scrum Master (25-member team)
  • Duration: December 2024 to February 2025

sections.title: Competitions and hackathons
sections.content: Keerthi has an extensive background in hackathons and Capture The Flag (CTF) events, accumulating over INR 50,000 in prize winnings across various competitions.

subsections.title: Hackathons and coding contests
subsections.content:
{{image:images/codevita.jpg|TCS CodeVita Season 13|right|300}}

Keerthi has secured multiple podium finishes. In October 2026, she was the runner-up in the Fun Quiz at the Major League Hacking × OS Community × Sapiens Campus Hacktoberfest Meetup. In May 2026, she won the Portfolio Building Challenge at CodeSapiens Summer Fest. Also in 2026, she was named the Best Women Coder Runner-up at TCS CodeVita Season 13, an achievement highlighted in the Times of India{{ref:toi}}. In December 2025, she won the RootSprout Build From Scratch event with Yapformer. She also placed as the Second Runner-up at Defy'26 with a 5-member team for the project TimeCapsule.

{{image:images/neo.jpg|Neo Codeathon|left|220}}

In 2025, she won the AmpliCode Hackathon in a 2-member team with Aravind, where they first presented PhishMate, and in August 2024 she won the Neo Codeathon.

subsections.title: Capture The Flag
subsections.content:
{{image:images/clawctf.jpg|ClawCTF at Rendezvous 2k26|right|300}}

In 2026, Keerthi took on a leadership role as an Organizer for ClawCTF at Rendezvous 2k26, successfully conducting a multi-domain CTF with over 60 registrations. The event's public repository organizes its challenges into 7 categories: AI, Cryptography, Forensics, Miscellaneous, OSINT, Reverse Engineering and Web. It also holds the event's rules document and promotional posters.

{{image:images/exploitx.jpg|ExploitX CTF at CIT Chennai|left|260}}

Her CTF journey gained momentum during her second year, when in August 2025 she competed in the ExploitX CTF at CIT Chennai as part of team Yakuza with her teammate Joshni. The team ranked 7th in the qualifiers and emerged as top performers in the finals.

In March 2025, she won the Binary Breakout event at ReVil'25 as part of a 4-member team.

subsections.title: Writing, video and drawing competitions
subsections.content:
{{image:images/shebuilds.jpg|SheBuilds Octocat Drawing Competition|right|300}}

Beyond technical events, Keerthi has won a writing competition held by her college's language club and a short video-making competition held by its eco club. In December 2024, she was also the second runner-up in the Octocat Drawing Competition at SheBuilds.

sections.title: Projects
sections.content: Keerthi has developed several notable projects, many of which can be found on her GitHub profile{{ref:github}}.

subsections.title: ViewLing
subsections.content:
ViewLing{{ref:viewling}}, requested by her father, is an ongoing web application designed to visualize exported WhatsApp messages. According to its to-do list, the app already supports multiple chat files, message dates, a light and dark theme toggle, messages to yourself, clickable links, PDF attachments, drag-and-drop uploads, colored senders in group chats, and closing a chat with the Esc key.

  • Implemented: multiple file support, date support, theme toggle, link support, PDF files, drag and drop, group chat colors
  • Planned: message search, edited, deleted, pinned and forwarded messages, formatted text, more media types (audio, GIF, PowerPoint, Excel, contact cards), live location, sticky dates, reduced lag on long chats and wider device support

subsections.title: TimeCapsule
subsections.content:
{{video:https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82693a46-e0b0-4533-bd7b-625afaf00082|TimeCapsule decentralized archive.|right}}

TimeCapsule{{ref:timecapsule}} was inspired by a petition to save the centralized Wayback Machine from being shut down over copyright disputes. Keerthi created a tamper-proof, decentralized internet archive using SHA-256, OpenTimestamps, and IPFS to ensure web history cannot be easily erased or censored. Its repository describes it as a decentralized digital notary for the web, built by Team Web Wizards.

The project targets 3 weaknesses of the web: link rot, takedowns of centralized archives, and content that is quietly edited or faked with screenshots. A server-side browser captures a forensic snapshot of a page, the content is uploaded to IPFS, and its SHA-256 hash is anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain through OpenTimestamps. Anyone can verify a capture by downloading the evidence file and its .ots proof and checking them at OpenTimestamps.org.

  • Features: forensic web capture (HTML, metadata and screenshots via Puppeteer), drag-and-drop file timestamping, Bitcoin-anchored .ots receipts, MetaMask sign-in, public and private vaults, and PDF chain-of-custody reports
  • Technologies: SHA-256, OpenTimestamps, IPFS, Next.js 15, Tailwind CSS, Supabase, PostgreSQL (Prisma), Puppeteer
  • Recognition: Second runner-up, Defy'26 (January 2026), as a 5-member team

subsections.title: Yapformer
subsections.content:
{{video:https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f6f1d3b-4388-4657-a99c-e4b7251e04f8|Yapformer demonstration.|left}}

YapFormer{{ref:yapformer}} is a GPT-style transformer language model built from scratch in Python and PyTorch. Keerthi built the command-line user interface used to interact with the model; the model itself, including its architecture and training, is the work of the repository's author, Shri Sai Aravind. It was submitted to the RootSprout Build From Scratch event in December 2025, where it won.

For context, the underlying model has about 56 million parameters and was trained for 15,000 steps (roughly 4.5 hours) on the TinyStories dataset, using techniques such as rotary embeddings, grouped query attention, key–value caching, RMSNorm and SwiGLU layers. Despite its small size, it produces short stories of surprisingly high quality.

  • Keerthi's role: command-line user interface
  • Model technologies: Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face (datasets and tokenization)

subsections.title: ParamStock
subsections.content: ParamStock, developed at the request of her father, is an ongoing project: a real-time stock monitoring and WhatsApp alert system built using Flask and Twilio, currently tracking more than 10 stocks.

subsections.title: KeerthiOS
subsections.content: KeerthiOS is Keerthi's earlier, terminal-based portfolio website, first published in May 2025 and built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Because non-technical visitors can find a terminal interface hard to navigate, she later created KeerthiWIKI, the encyclopedia-style site you are reading now, as an easier-to-browse version of the same portfolio.

subsections.title: PhishMate
subsections.content:
{{video:https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b57aeccb-8807-46a8-b8cd-6ac134825d86|PhishMate extension demonstration.|left}}

PhishMate{{ref:phishmate}} was initially built during an early hackathon with Shri Sai Aravind, combining Aravind's focus on AI with Keerthi's focus on cybersecurity. The AI-powered browser extension detects phishing attempts with about 90% accuracy using fully local analysis. It later evolved into PhishMateBERT{{ref:phishmatebert}} as her honors capstone project.

PhishMate checks emails in real time inside Chromium-based browsers. A custom-trained BERT model analyzes the email text for common red flags such as urgency, poor grammar and requests for personal information, while the links in the message are extracted and their IP addresses are checked against AbuseIPDB as a second layer of defense. The model was trained on about 8,000 emails and reached roughly 90% accuracy on its test set. Because the model runs on a local Flask API, email content never leaves the user's device, and only IP addresses are sent for the reputation check.

{{video:https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf451bc5-b982-4bd9-8d50-1e05b4ecc037|PhishMateBERT extension demonstration.|right}}

PhishMateBERT replaces the AbuseIPDB link check with a fine-tuned DeBERTa classifier and removes the need for any third-party threat-intelligence service or API key. It serves predictions from a local API at 127.0.0.1, shows email and detection counters in a light or dark popup, and its manifest covers Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo Mail, Proton Mail, Zoho Mail, iCloud Mail, AOL Mail, GMX Mail and Yandex Mail.

  • Technologies: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, Flask
  • Evaluation: about 90% accuracy on its test set of roughly 8,000 emails, with fully local analysis
  • Roadmap: Firefox support, a more robust model trained on a larger dataset, and additional sources for checking malicious links
  • Recognition: Winner, AmpliCode Hackathon (June 2025), as a 2-member team with Aravind

subsections.title: Password Manager
subsections.content:
Password Manager{{ref:passwordmanager}} is the MySQL-backed, terminal-based tool she built for her HSC practicals. It lets a user store, view and manage login credentials (username, password and website) through a numbered text menu, and was designed as a beginner-level project to demonstrate database handling and basic CRUD operations. Its repository notes that it is a learning project and should not be used to store real passwords without encryption.

  • Features: add credentials, list all entries, search by username, delete a specific entry, clear the whole database, and handle invalid input
  • Technologies: Python 3, MySQL Connector for Python, MySQL
  • Schema: a single password_manager table with username, password and website columns

sections.title: Personal life
sections.content:
Outside of her professional and academic pursuits, Keerthi tries to do 1 LeetCode a day to "keep her reasoning in play". She is actively looking to enter the field of bug bounty.

Keerthi considers herself a person with a lot of hobbies, from drawing, painting, writing and origami to photography, video editing, reading, movies and music. She also enjoys badminton, Genshin Impact, Skribbl and Minecraft, and is fond of stickers.
